 State Of Gujarat
 Versus
 Laxmilal Mangilal Shah & Ors.
 ========================================================
 Appearance:
 Ms.C.M.Shah, App for the Appellant(s) No. 1
 Mr Dk Modi(1317) for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 1,2,3,4
 Mr Md Modi(1318) for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 1,2,3,4

 Oral Judgment

1. This appeal has been filed by the appellant - State under Section 378(1)(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Code') against the order passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Olpad NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1070/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined (hereinafter referred to as 'the learned Trial Court') in Criminal Case No. 1194 of 1987 on 31.12.2010, whereby, the learned Trial Court has acquitted the respondents - original accused nos. 1 to 4 from the offences punishable under Section 7(1)(2)(5) and Rules 32 and State Of Gujarat vs Laxmilal Mangilal Shah on 20 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75751844/
1 62 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act').
1.1.

sentences.text: As accused nos. 8 to 10 were not remaining present before the Court and as the proceedings were not being conducted, an order for a separate trial qua the accused nos. 8, 9, and 10 was passed and the trial proceeded against the accused nos. 1 to 7.

The accused no. 3 - M/s. Modi and Co. is a partnership firm and the accused nos. 4 to 7 are the partners of the accsued no. 3 - firm, out of which, during pendency of the trial, accused no. 5 - Chimanlal Chhotalal Modi, accused no.6 - Kanchanben Chhaganlal Modi and accused no. 7 - Hiralal Chhotalal Modi expired, and hence, the Trial against the accused nos. 5 to 7 was abated by an order of the learned Trial Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1070/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined 1.2.
The respondents are hereinafter referred to as 'the accused' as they stood in the rank and file in the original case, for the sake of convenience, clarity and brevity.

2. The relevant facts leading to filing of the present appeal are as under:
2.1.

On 21.05.1987, at around 15:00 hours, the complainant, Food Inspector Ashwinkumar Manubhai Shah, visited the shop of "Shri Lakshmi Kirana Stores",
situated in the Market of village Kim, Taluka Olpad and after the necessary procedure, a sample of groundnut oil from a sealed packed tin was taken.

The accused no.1 gave the bill of M/s Modi and Co., village Mosali, Taluka Mangrol from where he had purchased the sealed tin of groundnut, which was produced by "M/s.
Lakshmi Oil Industries", village Jasdan, District Rajkot.

After the due procedure, the sample was sent to the Public Analyst, and as per the report of the Public Analyst, the sample of groundnut oil did not conform to the standards and provisions laid down under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1070/2011 JUDGMENT DATED:
20/08/2025 undefined hence, a complaint was filed before the Court of the Judicial Magistrate,
First Class, Olpad under Sections 7(i) and 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

2.2. The accused nos. 1 to 7 were duly served with the summons and the accused nos. 1 to 7 appeared before the learned Trial Court and it was verified whether the copies of the papers were provided to the accused as per the provisions of Section 207 of the Code.
The accused nos. 5 to 7 expired during the trial and hence, the case qua the accused nos. 5 to 7 was abated by the order of the learned Trial Court.

The accused nos. 1 to 4 preferred a pursis at Exh.54 inviting the learned Trial Court to frame a charge against them and accordingly, a charge was framed by the learned Trial Court at Exh.82 and the statements of the accused were recorded at Exh.83 to Exh. 86 respectively, wherein, the accused denied all the contents of the charge and the entire evidence of the prosecution was taken on record.

The prosecution examined 2 witnesses i.e. the complainant - Ashwinkumar Manubhai Shah at Exh.101 and PW- 2 Ahmedbhai Daoodbhai Patel at Exh.158 and produced 29 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1070/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined documentary evidences were produced in support of the case.
2.3. After the evidence of the complainant was closed, the further statement of the accused under Section 313 of the Code were recorded wherein in the accused denied the evidence on record.

After hearing the arguments of the learned APP and State Of Gujarat vs Laxmilal Mangilal Shah on 20 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75751844/
2 learned advocate for the accused and after perusing the documents on record, the learned Trial Court, by the impugned judgment and order, was pleased to acquit the accused for the offences punishable under Section 7(i) of the Act.
3. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned Trial Court

entities.text: State Of Gujarat vs Laxmilal Mangilal Shah
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the appellant - State has filed the present appeal mainly stating that the impugned judgment and order of acquittal passed by the learned Trial Court is contrary to law, evidence on record and principles of natural justice.

The learned Trial Court has erred in evaluating the evidence on record of the case and without appreciating the evidence in its real perspective, has acquitted NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1070/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined the accused.

There are direct and indirect evidence connecting the respondent with the crime which are produced in the Court and in spite of the fact, the learned Trial Court, without appreciating the oral as well as documentary evidence on record of the case, straight way arrived at a conclusion that the prosecution has failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt.
The learned Trial Court has erred in not considering the evidence of the complainant and other witnesses which has fully supported the case of the prosecution.

The learned Trial Court has passed the impugned judgment and order of acquittal without giving any cogent and convincing reasons and the same is illegal, invalid and improper, and therefore, the same requires to be quashed and set aside.
4. Heard learned APP Ms.C.M.Shah for the appellant - State and learned advocate Mr.D.K.Modi for the respondent nos. 1 - 4.
Perused the impugned judgment and order of acquittal and have re-appreciated the entire evidence of the prosecution on record of the case.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1070/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined 5.

Learned APP Ms.C.M.Shah for the appellant - State has taken this Court through the entire evidence produced by the prosecution and has vehemently argued that the learned Trial Court has not appreciated the evidence properly and the prosecution has produced cogent evidence to prove the case and has successfully proved the case against the accused but the learned Trial Court has not considered the same and has acquitted the accused.
The judgment and order of acquittal passed by the learned Judge is contrary to law, evidence on record and principles of justice.
The judgment and order of acquittal passed by learned Judge is based on inferences, not warranted by facts of the case and also on presumptions, not permitted by law.
Learned APP has urged this Court to quash and set aside the impugned judgment and order of acquittal and to find the accused guilty for the said offence and impose maximum sentence on the accused.

6. Learned advocate Mr.D.K.Modi for the respondent nos. 1 to 4 has submitted that the learned Trial Court has appreciated all the evidence in true perspective and has not NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1070/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined committed any error in acquitting the accused.
Therefore, no interference of this Court is required in the impugned judgment and the order of acquittal passed by the learned Trial Court and has urged this Court to reject the appeal.

State Of Gujarat vs Laxmilal Mangilal Shah on 20 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75751844/
3 7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is a settled principle of law that in an appeal against acquittal, the Appellate Court is circumscribed by limitation that no interference has to be made in the order of acquittal unless after appreciation of the evidence produced before the learned Trial Court, it appears that there are some manifest illegality or perversity which could not have been possibly arrived at by the Court.

It is also a settled principle that there is no embargo on the Appellate Court to review the evidence but,
generally the order of acquittal shall not be interfered with as the presumption of innocence of the accused is further strengthened by the order of acquittal.

The golden thread which runs through the web of administration of justice in criminal cases is that if two views are possible on the evidence adduced in the case of the prosecution i.e. (i) guilt of the accused and (ii) his innocence, the view,
which is in favour of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1070/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined the accused, should be adopted, and if the trial Court has taken the view in favour of the accused, the Appellate Court should not disturb the findings of the acquittal.

The Appellate Court can interfere with the judgment and order of acquittal only when there are compelling and substantial reasons and the order is clearly unreasonable and where the Appellate Court comes to conclusion that based on the evidence, the conviction is a must.
8.

In light of the above, the evidence produced by the prosecution on record is appreciated and the prosecution has examined PW-1 Ashwinkumar Manubhai Shah at Exh.101 and the witness is the Food Inspector and complainant, who has narrated the entire procedure that he had undertaken at the time of taking the sample, and thereafter, and has produced all the necessary documents in support of his case.

The complainant has produced 29 documentary evidences including his appointment letter at Exh.102, certificate at Exh.103, copy of the Gazette at Exh. 104, Form No.6 at Exh.105, receipt of the amount paid at Exh.106, the cover, which was on the tin of groundnut oil at Exh.107, the Panchama at Exh.108, forwarding NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1070/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined letter sent to the Public Analyst at Exh.109,
Memorandum Form No.8 at Exh. 110, receipts received from the Public Analyst that the samples were received at Exh.111 and Exh.112, the forwarding letter, by which, the samples were sent to the Local Health Authority at Exh.113, a letter written to the warrantor M/s. Modi and Co. at Exh. 114,
Form No. 6 at Exh.115 and the other documents, by which, the letters were sent through R.P.A.D. to the producer "M/s.Lakshmi Oil Industries" and the report of the Public Analyst at Exh.124.
The complainant has also produced the letter seeking permission to file the complaint at Exh.126 and the license of the accused no.1 at Exh.149 and Exh.150.

During the cross-examination by the learned advocate for the accused, the complainant has admitted that the tin, from which, the sample was taken was a sealed tin and he did not stir the contents completely.
The bottles, in which, the samples were given to him from the office and he does not know who had cleaned the bottles and whether they were without moisture.

He cannot say whether the bottles were clean and dry and without moisture and he cannot say whether the competent authority has NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1070/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined read all the documents and has thereafter given the sanction to file the complaint.
After the sample was taken and prior to making the sample in three parts, it was not stirred and the tin, from which, the sample was taken was not tampered.

The vendor had given the documents, from which, he had purchased the sealed tin from the distributor and he did not meet any of the partners of the distributor and was not ready to examine any witness to show that the bottles were clean, dry and without moisture.

State Of Gujarat vs Laxmilal Mangilal Shah on 20 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75751844/
4 8.1. PW-2, Ahmedbhai Dawoodbhai Patel, examined at Exh.158, is the panch witness and has not supported the case of the prosecution and has been declared hostile and even during the cross-examination, he has not stated that the sample was taken by the Food Inspector in his presence.
9. On minute appreciation of the entire evidence of the prosecution, as per the case of the Food Inspector, the sample was taken from a sealed tin and prior to taking of the sample, the Food Inspector did not stir the contents of the tin properly.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1070/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined Even after the sample was taken and prior to making three parts of the sample, it was not stirred properly and the same is admitted by the Food Inspector in the cross-examination.

entities.text: State Of Gujarat vs Laxmilal Mangilal Shah
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, there is nothing on record to suggest that the bottles, in which, the samples were taken were clean, dry and without moisture and the Food Inspector PW-1 Ashwinkumar Manubhai Shah did not know who had cleaned and made the bottles dry from the office and no such witness has been examined by him before the learned Trial Court.

Moreover, PW-1 Ashwinkumar Manubhai Shah has also admitted that the tin, from which, the sample was taken was not tampered by the accused, who were selling the same and there is no mention as to whether the documents were actually considered prior to giving the sanction for filing of the complaint.
The learned Trial Court has concluded that the mandatory provisions of Rule-14 were breached and not followed properly and has passed the impugned judgment and order.

10. In view of the above, the learned trial Court has appreciated the entire evidence in proper perspective and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1070/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined there does not appear to be any infirmity and illegality in the impugned judgment and order of acquittal.

The learned Trial Court has appreciated all the evidence and this Court is of the considered opinion that the learned Trial Court was completely justified in acquitting the accused of the charges leveled against them.
This Court finds no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and order and the present appeal is devoid of merits and resultantly, the same is dismissed.

11. The impugned order passed in Criminal Case No.1194 of 1987 by the learned Judicial Magistrate,
First Class, Olpad on 31.12.2010 is hereby confirmed.
12. Bail bond stands cancelled.
Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Trial Court forthwith.

Sd/-
